To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FDI spillover effects are positive, significant, and are not limited geographically, but are more pronounced when foreign affiliates are oriented to the domestic, rather than the export market.

(i) FDI spillover effects are more likely to be found through backward linkages; (ii) the magnitude of these spillovers is significant, but it is lower than the estimates reported in earlier studies; and (iii) the effects are more pronounced when the foreign presence is concentrated in the domestic market
(a) foreign affiliates in downstream sectors generate productivity spillovers through their local suppliers; and (b) these spillovers do not depend on the degree of ownership of foreign investors.
